Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Concours d'Elegance Singapore – 13–16 August, IMBA Theatre

2. Orchard Road Fashion Week – 12–16 August

3. Sentosa GrillFest – final weekend, closes 16 August

4. Origin Grill's Kaviari Caviar Experience – 14 August

5. Hungry Ghost Festival begins – 13 August

6. Park90 – new home at Pan Pacific Orchard

7. PIE overnight closure – 16 August

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Origin Grill hosts a one-night-only collaboration this week, pairing its kitchen with Kaviari, the Paris-based caviar house, for a menu built entirely around showcasing their selections – not the usual single caviar course as a garnish, but the star ingredient across a full six-course dinner.

  • Origin Grill Presents: The Kaviari Caviar Experience – six-course set dinner curated by Chef Isaac Giam and Chef Simon Bell, paired with premium seasonal ingredients. SGD 188++ with a glass of champagne. Friday, 14 August 2026, 7:00pm.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

J65's Turkish guest-chef theme continues through the rest of August.

  • J65: Flavours of Türkiye – from $88++/adult. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off. Running throughout August.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Overall Summary

This is the last full weekend for Sentosa GrillFest before it closes on the 16th – make sure any guest who's been meaning to go gets a direct nudge this week. Orchard Road turns into a runway for its inaugural Fashion Week (12–16 August), while across town, IMBA Theatre hosts Singapore's first immersive Concours d'Elegance, bringing rare classic and exotic cars into cinematic, Grand Touring-style backdrops. The Hungry Ghost Festival also begins this week (13 August) – a good moment to prep the team on the cultural context, since guests will start noticing incense, joss paper offerings and empty front-row seats at outdoor performances around the island. On the Shangri-La side, Origin Grill's one-night Kaviari collaboration on the 14th is worth flagging early, as this kind of one-off dinner tends to fill up fast.

Events & Festivals

Concours d'Elegance Singapore

Singapore's first immersive Concours d'Elegance brings together rare classic, vintage and exotic automobiles – not displayed in a static hall, but surrounded by cinematic projections inspired by legendary Grand Touring routes like the Alps, Tuscany and the Stelvio Pass. VIP Preview and Preview ticket-holders watch the live judging on 13 August, before the winning cars go on public display from 14–16 August. Car meets run from IMBA Theatre to Dempsey Hill on 14 and 15 August, alongside talks, workshops and luxury brand showcases.

Event Date: 13–16 August 2026

Time: 10:00am–8:00pm

Location: IMBA Theatre (West Lawn, beside Bayfront Plaza), Gardens by the Bay

Admission: From S$29

Website: concourssg.com

Best For: Car Enthusiasts / Design Lovers / Something Different

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for guests with any interest in cars or design – the cinematic staging sets it apart from a typical static car show, and it's a genuinely new event for Singapore this year.

Orchard Road Fashion Week

The inaugural Orchard Road Fashion Week brings 25 runway shows over five days, uniting emerging designers and global labels for a first-of-its-kind season on Orchard Road. Each day runs five show blocks back to back, featuring a mix of Singaporean, regional and international designers and fashion schools.

Event Dates & Times: 12–16 August 2026, daily show blocks at 12:00–1:00pm, 2:00–3:00pm, 4:00–5:00pm, 6:00–7:00pm and 8:00–9:00pm

Location: *SCAPE The Ground Theatre, 2 Orchard Link, Singapore 237978

Admission: Ticketed – Front Row (VIP, limited to 100 passes per show), All Access Pass (2nd row, all 25 shows across the 5 days, limited to 100 passes total), Gold Pass (3rd row, all shows on a selected day, limited to 100 per day), Silver Pass (4th row, single show, limited to 30 per show)

Website: eventbrite.sg (search “Orchard Road Fashion Week”)

Best For: Fashion Enthusiasts / Young Adults / Something Different

Concierge Recommendation: Worth flagging to fashion-minded guests, though tickets for the higher tiers are limited – advise booking as soon as possible if they're keen on a specific show, and confirm which of the five daily time slots suits their schedule before booking.

Sentosa GrillFest – Final Weekend

Sentosa's beachfront cookout wraps up for the year this week. Same format that's made it a strong recommendation all summer – 42 food vendors across five zones, plus Chef's Grill, an eight-course omakase-style dinner served on the sand.

Event Date: Closes 16 August 2026

Time: 4:00pm–10:30pm

Location: Siloso Beach, Sentosa

Best For: Couples / Groups / Food Lovers / Sunset Diners

Concierge Recommendation: This is genuinely the last chance – make sure every guest who's shown any interest gets a direct, final nudge this week rather than a passing mention.

Restaurants & Bars

Park90

Previously located at Conrad Singapore Orchard, Park90 has relocated to Pan Pacific Orchard's lush 11th-floor Garden Terrace – a sophisticated wine bar blending modern luxury with nature. Guests can choose the contemporary indoor salon or the breezy alfresco terrace, with a world-class wine programme paired with artisanal bar snacks like cheese platters and duck.

Location: Pan Pacific Orchard, 10 Claymore Road, Level 11 Garden Terrace, Singapore 229540

Reservation Policy: Call to reconfirm hours and booking policy directly with the hotel

Best For: Couples / Wine Lovers / Business Travellers / Rooftop Views

Concierge Recommendation: A relaxed, elevated option for guests wanting wine and small bites without a full dinner commitment – the alfresco terrace is worth requesting specifically on a clear evening.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two more picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Lei Garden

Unlike other branches in the Lei Garden group, the CHIJMES outlet has a European decor echoing the colonial style of the building that houses it – a striking setting for what's otherwise a very traditional Cantonese fine-dining menu. New dishes are added regularly, and the kitchen has held a Michelin star continuously since 2016.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required; phone, email or WhatsApp to book. Groups above 14 must call directly.

Hours: Daily, 11:30am–3:00pm & 6:00pm–11:00pm

Contact: +65 6339 3822 / +65 9710 1768 (WhatsApp) / chijmes@leigardengroup.com

Address: 30 Victoria Street, #01-24 CHIJMES, Singapore 187996

Dress Code: Smart and Elegant

Concierge Recommendation: A reliable, elegant choice for guests wanting refined Cantonese cuisine without needing to venture far from the Civic District.

Shinji by Kanesaka

A pioneer of authentic omakase dining in Singapore since 2010, now consolidated into a single location at The St Regis Singapore. Head Chef Keiichi Kobayashi has spent more than three decades refining the same Edo-style tradition, and the restaurant has held a Michelin star for years running. The format is intimate by design – a direct, unhurried exchange between guest and chef at the sushi counter.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: No credit card required for standard bookings; call ahead, especially for weekend lunch or dinner. Closed Sundays.

Hours: Mon–Sat, 12:00pm–3:00pm & 6:00pm–10:30pm. Closed Sunday.

Contact: +65 6884 8239

Address: The St Regis Singapore, 29 Tanglin Road, Singapore 247911

Signature: Lunch omakase from $125 (12 pieces); Yuki set $180; Yume omakase set $250 (sushi and cooked dishes)

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable special-occasion recommendation for sushi purists – remind guests it's closed Sundays before they plan around it.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

PIE Overnight Closure – 16 August

Stretches of the PIE and adjoining roads near Potong Pasir/Bendemeer will close overnight from 12:00am to 5:00am on 16 August, for the same bridge-launching works that caused closures on 2 August. Motorists on PIE heading toward Changi will be diverted via Exit 15 through Braddell Road and Upper Serangoon Road during this window. This is expected to be the final date in this series of closures.

Downtown Line Night Works

Downtown Line trains continue stopping earlier on Friday nights (last train around 11:30pm) and starting later on Saturday mornings (from 8:30am), until 5 September. Free shuttle buses run 5:00–8:30am Saturdays, connecting Bukit Panjang, Bugis, MacPherson and Expo stations.

Hungry Ghost Festival – Background & Cultural Notes

The Hungry Ghost Festival (also known as Zhong Yuan Jie) falls during the seventh month of the Lunar calendar – 13 August to 10 September this year, with Ghost Day itself on 27 August. Tradition holds that the gates of the afterlife open on the first day of the seventh month, allowing spirits to roam the living world until the month ends. The festival blends Buddhist and Taoist traditions that developed in China over many centuries: the Buddhist Ullambana observance, centred on filial piety and easing the suffering of ancestors, merged over time with the Taoist Zhongyuan festival honouring wandering spirits with no living descendants to care for them. It's often compared to Mexico's Día de Muertos or North America's Halloween – a tradition of remembering and paying respect to the deceased, rather than something to be alarmed by.

During this period, guests may notice incense and joss paper burning near roadsides and void decks, small food offerings left in public areas, and getai (outdoor stage) performances with empty front-row seats reserved for spirits, by tradition. None of this affects transport or access, but a brief, respectful explanation helps guests understand what they're seeing rather than feel confused or alarmed by it.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Airport traffic remains elevated through the peak August travel period. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Hungry Ghost Festival Continues

Runs through 10 September, with Ghost Day itself falling on 27 August – expect the cultural observances noted above to continue and intensify slightly around that date.

POP TOY SHOW (PTS) Singapore

POP MART's flagship pop-culture toy and collectibles event lands 21–23 August at Sands Expo & Convention Centre – worth watching for guests who enjoyed the CRYBABY activation and might be interested in a bigger collector event.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Sentosa GrillFest closes 16 August – this is the final call, not just a reminder. Flag it directly to any guest who's shown interest.

  • Origin Grill's Kaviari Experience (14 August) is a one-night dinner – advise guests to book early rather than assume walk-in availability.

  • Shinji by Kanesaka is closed on Sundays – confirm this before recommending it for a Sunday dinner.

  • The Hungry Ghost Festival begins 13 August – a brief, respectful heads-up helps guests who encounter incense, offerings or getai performances understand the context rather than feel confused.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Last Call for GrillFest

Afternoon: Sentosa Express or cable car over, then A Magical Island Adventure character meet-and-greets.

Evening: Sentosa GrillFest on Siloso Beach – arrive for sunset, since this is the final weekend.

Tip: Book Chef's Grill ahead if guests want the omakase-style dinner – it will likely sell out for the closing weekend.

Full Day — Cars, Culture & Cuisine

Morning: Gardens by the Bay, then Concours d'Elegance at IMBA Theatre.

Afternoon: Walk to Marina Bay Sands and the Helix Bridge for skyline views.

Evening: Dinner at Lei Garden in the Civic District, or Shinji by Kanesaka for sushi (not Sunday).

Tip: IMBA Theatre and Marina Bay Sands are a comfortable 10–15 minute walk apart – no need to arrange transport between them.

2 Days — Orchard & Sentosa

Day 1

Morning: Orchard Road shopping. Afternoon: Catch a runway show at Orchard Road Fashion Week (*SCAPE), or Park90 for an early wine and cheese. Evening: Dinner at Rang Mahal or Candlenut.

Day 2

Morning to Afternoon: Sentosa – CRYBABY photo stops, The Portals Experience if still in Orchard the day before instead. Evening: Sentosa GrillFest, final weekend.

Tip: If guests are torn between Fashion Week and Concours d'Elegance, ask about their interests first – the two events draw quite different crowds and are on opposite sides of town.

Quick Reference

Best Last-Chance Pick: Sentosa GrillFest (closes 16 August)

Best New Event: Concours d'Elegance Singapore

Best Fashion Pick: Orchard Road Fashion Week

Best New Restaurant: Park90

Best Special-Occasion Dining: Shinji by Kanesaka

Best Civic District Dining: Lei Garden

Best One-Night Dining Experience: Origin Grill's Kaviari Caviar Experience
